headline: Strong inflows and fee growth lift earnings
summary_short: BlackRock reported Q3 2026 revenue of $7.75B (+19.1% y/y), GAAP diluted EPS of $10.57 and as-adjusted EPS of $15.93 (+37.9%), with $205B of net inflows.
summary_long: Revenue rose 19% y/y to $7.75B on higher markets, organic base fee growth, higher performance fees and 14% growth in technology services and subscription revenue. As-adjusted operating income rose 27% to $3.33B at a 47.8% margin. GAAP diluted EPS was $10.57, affected by a noncash change in the fair value of contingent consideration that is excluded from as-adjusted results. Net inflows were $205B in the quarter, including $135B into iShares ETFs, taking AUM to $15.5T. BlackRock repurchased $550M of shares.
confidence_notes: The shard's Q3 EPS of 15.93 is the as-adjusted (non-GAAP) figure, while its prior-period values are SEC GAAP basic EPS, so shard prior values are not comparable; all deltas here use the release's own same-basis y/y comparatives (GAAP $8.43, as adjusted $11.55). GAAP and as-adjusted results differ mainly because of a noncash change in the fair value of contingent consideration and other acquisition-related items. Total net flows of $205.5B vs $204.6B a year ago are essentially flat, so direction is flat. The release gives no numeric guidance.

drivers.explanation: The CEO points to broad net inflows across asset classes and regions, iShares strength, systematic active equities, private markets and technology momentum from Aladdin.
Reflects the positive impact of markets, organic base fee growth, higher performance fees, and higher technology services and subscription revenue.
GAAP EPS growth was affected by a noncash change in fair value of contingent consideration tied to prior acquisitions, which is excluded from as-adjusted results.
As-adjusted EPS growth of 38% also reflects higher nonoperating income in the current quarter on top of the 27% rise in as-adjusted operating income.
Net inflows were $205B in the quarter, with $135B into iShares ETFs and $66B into active strategies, led by fixed income and systematic franchises.
